question: Can instruction models preserve recipient scope, exception, modality and version applicability when checking a Korean policy claim against supplied evidence?
scope: A specified claim and selected condition only, not whole eligibility or legal advice. Supported / contradicted / not established are semantic labels; system abstention is measured separately.
stages: Build and freeze authored development probes; run two local instruction models with the same baseline prompt.
Inspect development failures, implement a scope/evidence refinement and freeze all methods before scoring new inputs.
Collect complete new official revision documents and author claim/evidence annotations without inspecting test predictions. Record pre-existing search-snippet exposure.
Run frozen methods on new source-backed and separately authored composition probes. Preserve every first output, no silent correction or model-dependent sample selection.
Audit evidence removal, irrelevant-clause perturbation and source-version selection. Verify saved outputs and publish honest results.
runtime: Existing local Ollama service, model digests recorded, Q4_K_M weights, explicit prompts and decoding options. No cloud API or new model training.
limits: AI-authored probes and AI-assisted official references, no independent human gold standard. New prompts are tuned on development only. Synthetic split shares an author and conceptual categories; it does not establish population generalization. Public-source contamination of model pretraining cannot be excluded.
metrics: paired consistency under evidence removal and distractors
source_selection: Prefer complete original and revised official documents. Jeju 2025 maternity-benefit revision is a fixed target found before implementation; its search excerpts were seen. Other sources must be selected before their predictions. Do not label revised notices as explicit typo corrections without evidence.
publication: Public code, generated examples, claim annotations, short source metadata/locators and outputs. Full official documents and full extracted source inputs remain outside Git. Do not publish local model filesystem paths or third-party operational settings.
